title: Anatomic Landmark-Based Measurement of the Achilles Tendon
author: Daniel Urness
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beaejabe
materials: Mark above location with marking pen.

steps.title: Position subject on framing square
steps.instruction: Seat the subject upright with the hip flexed, abducted, and externally rotated so the lateral side of the lower leg lies flat on the framing square outline; align the plantar foot with the square base and the posterior calf with the vertical side to create a 90° ankle angle.

steps.title: Measure gastrocnemius‑to‑heel distance (anatomic)
steps.instruction: With the subject in the above position, palpate the step‑off where the medial head of the gastrocnemius becomes the Achilles tendon, mark the spot with a marking pen, measure from this mark to the base of the non‑compressed heel pad using a tape measure, record the value, then remove the pen mark with an alcohol pad. Repeat this measurement three times on each leg (total six measurements) and have each rater rotate to the next subject until all raters have recorded measurements for every subject.

substeps.instruction: Mark the location with a marking pen.
Measure to the base of the non‑compressed heel pad with a tape measure and record.
Remove the pen mark with an alcohol pad.
Repeat three times per leg (six total).
Rotate subjects to the next rater until all raters have measured each subject.

steps.title: Collect ultrasound landmark measurements
steps.instruction: Position the subject exactly as for the anatomic technique, use ultrasound to locate the confluence of the medial gastrocnemius head and Achilles tendon, mark this point (the authors placed a paper clip on the ultrasound image then marked the area with a marking pen), measure from the mark to the base of the non‑compressed heel pad with a tape measure, record the value, remove the pen mark with an alcohol pad, and repeat three times on each leg (six total). Rotate subjects to the next rater until each rater has recorded measurements for every subject.

substeps.instruction: Identify the gastrocnemius‑Achilles confluence with ultrasound.
Mark the landmark (paper clip on image, then marking pen).
Measure to the base of the non‑compressed heel pad with a tape measure and record.
Remove the pen mark with an alcohol pad.
Repeat three times per leg (six total).
Rotate subjects to the next rater until all raters have measured each subject.

steps.title: Position patient for MRI scanning
steps.instruction: Place the patient supine in the MRI scanner with both ankles positioned at 90°.

steps.title: Acquire MRI image series
steps.instruction: Obtain axial, coronal, and sagittal T1 series covering both legs, ensuring each image captures the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the distalmost portion of the non‑compressed heel pad.

steps.title: Identify MRI landmarks and measure distance
steps.instruction: Using an axial cut, locate the confluence of the medial gastrocnemius head with the Achilles tendon and confirm the landmark on a sagittal or coronal image; then, on the coronal or sagittal view, locate the distalmost portion of the non‑compressed heel pad and measure the distance between the two landmarks with imaging software. Each leg is measured once by two separate raters.

substeps.instruction: Identify the gastrocnemius‑Achilles confluence on an axial slice and locate the corresponding point on a sagittal or coronal slice.
Identify the distalmost non‑compressed heel pad on a coronal or sagittal slice.
Measure the distance between the two landmarks using the imaging software.
Repeat the measurement once per leg by a second rater.
